overall: Opus 5 reviewed the 26,649-byte brief, plan, delta spec, and build blueprint through Drydock's structured-output-only peer adapter. It found the governance intent unusually honest but returned four load-bearing architecture blockers: same-user Windows process separation did not enforce the claimed credential confinement; token refresh/write behavior was undecided and could invalidate Claude Code sessions; task cost in tokens had no evidenced conversion to quota-window percentage; and fixed-reset arithmetic was applied without first-class fixed, sliding, or unknown window semantics.
blocking_concerns: Downgrade the same-user broker from hostile credential isolation to an anti-accidental-flow boundary, or specify a concrete stronger OS principal/service boundary that can still access the Claude credential.
Make the credential store read-only and convert expiry or 401 into unavailable; do not refresh, rotate, or write Claude credentials.
Remove cardinal task-affordability arithmetic until percent-per-task-class units are evidenced from separately proven sole-client intervals, or use ordinal routing.
Make fixed_reset, sliding, and unknown window kinds explicit; unknown semantics cannot contribute positive margin or reset-horizon claims.
gaps: Constrain window names, limitation codes, strings, and secret-shaped values at both broker and core boundaries.
Specify Windows Job Object cleanup, asynchronous pipe drain, byte bounds, UTF-8 handling, and failure evidence.
Serialize concurrent repositories through a machine-local lease and persist hard call budgets across restarts.
A bounded operational probe may only downgrade capacity and must share the circuit breaker.
Pin the private response schema and fail unavailable on drift.
Use one freshness policy with monotonic in-process age and bounded clock-skew handling.
Persist cache/history only outside repositories with bounded enum task classes and retention.
Replace checked design-intent acceptance boxes with unproven runtime gates.
Add private-endpoint permission and ToS acceptance to the Owner gate.
Resolve pilot pre-dispatch review versus automatic side-effect dispatch.
Evaluate a default-off feature flag before broker spawn or credential touch.
risks: A third-party widget suggests reachability but does not prove current endpoint availability or permission.
Credential-reading code expands Drydock's trusted computing base and supply-chain exposure.
Stale snapshots must be structurally unable to contribute headroom.
Sampling-to-dispatch TOCTOU remains and reserves must cover it conservatively.
Human split agreement in shadow dogfood measures agreement, not correctness.
required_changes: Correct the credential-boundary, refresh, scheduling-unit, and window-semantics blockers normatively.
Add strict snapshot value shapes, broker lifecycle mechanics, cross-instance admission, call caps, schema drift failure, freshness semantics, and bounded storage.
Keep the MVP recommendation-only with mandatory pilot review and structurally unallocatable reserves.
Correct evidentiary language and make the credential/private-endpoint Owner gates explicit.
